title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §7 of the notes). X is a space stratified by closed strata X_i (i in a poset I), with the frontier-type axiom (19): X_i ∩ X_j = ⋃_{k≤i,j} X_k. I_0 is the set of minimal indices and I* = I \ I_0. For each β in I_0 there is a tube T_β around X_β, with boundary Ṫ_β. X* is the space obtained by deleting the open tubes, stratified by X_i* (i in I*). I*_β = {i in I* | i ≥ β} is the set of strata that approach X_β.

Grothendieck compares two kinds of data:
- (17): the stratified space X together with tubular neighbourhoods of the minimal strata, transverse to the strata.
- (18): the 'dévissé' data. These are the stratified space X*, the boundaries Ṫ_β ⊂ X* fibred over X_β, and the gluing information, subject to conditions (20).

The previous page reduces axiom (19) for X to cases. The case i ≤ j uses condition (e). The case where i, j are incomparable and one lies in I_0 follows from (19).

This page finishes the case i, j ∈ I*. By the covering/locality property (4), it suffices to check X_i∩X_j∩T_β = ⋃_{k≤i,j} X_k∩T_β for every β (and on X*, where it is (f)). Only ⊂ needs proof. If the left side is empty there is nothing to prove. Otherwise X_i and X_j both meet T_β, so i, j ∈ I_β. The tube is a (mapping-cylinder/cone) bundle over X_β with fibre the cone on Ṫ_β ∩ fibre. So the identity follows from (f) restricted to Ṫ_β ⊂ X*, together with (19).

This yields the Proposition. Systems (17) satisfying the stratification axioms (H) and the transversality conditions are equivalent to systems (18) satisfying (20), plus (e), (f) saying that (X_i*)_{i∈I*} is a stratification of X*. This is a one-step 'dévissage': cutting out a conic neighbourhood of the minimal strata.

§8 'Conical structure on a stratified space' then begins. The setting is X stratified of type I, with given 'cylindrical' boundary pieces (B_α, ξ_α), transverse to each other and to the X_i. The next page defines a 'donnée de conicité' by recursion on card I. It consists of:
- (a) a strict conic neighbourhood T_{I_0} of the union of the minimal strata, transverse to the B_α;
- (b) a conical structure on the induced data on X*, in which the boundaries Ṫ_β = Ẋ_β are added as new cylindrical boundary pieces.

This is the recursive blow-up ('déploiement') of a stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object. It is the programme announced in the title and alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: No substantive error. The reduction via (4) to the pieces T_β and X* is sketched: the role of (4) as a covering/locality statement is assumed rather than stated on this page.

Minor gap: the step 'from (f) induced on Ṫ_β and (19)' relies implicitly on the conic/cylinder structure of T_β over X_β, so that a stratum meets T_β exactly as the cone over its trace on Ṫ_β. This is not written out.
The identification 'Ṫ_β = Ẋ_β' is notation for the boundary of the tube regarded as a new boundary stratum of X*, not literally the boundary of X_β.

ideas.what: Equivalence between a stratified space with a chosen transverse tube around the minimal strata, and the 'cut-open' data: the stratified complement X* together with the tube boundaries fibred over the minimal strata and the gluing conditions (one-step dévissage).
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / blow-up of a closed stratum; decomposition of a stratified space into a link bundle plus complement (Thom–Mather control data, Verona's 'resolution', Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzipping).
ideas.where_published: Only alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 (dévissage of stratified structures, 'déploiement').

ideas.what: Recursive definition (on card I) of a 'donnée de conicité': a strict conic neighbourhood of the minimal strata transverse to given cylindrical boundary pieces, plus inductively a conic structure on X* with the tube boundaries added as new boundary pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Recursive conical/control structure; inductive construction of a manifold with corners (déploiement) from a stratified space; conically smooth structures.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather (control data), Siebenmann (locally cone-like spaces, 1972), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (conically smooth stratified spaces, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces a 'théorème de dévissage' for tame stratified spaces in qualitative terms; the detailed recursion is not published.

ideas.what: Verification of the closed-strata axiom X_i∩X_j = ⋃_{k≤i,j} X_k by localization onto tubes T_β and the complement X*.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for poset-stratified spaces checked locally

missed.claim: The inductive 'cut out a conic neighbourhood of the minimal strata, then put a conic structure on the remainder with the tube boundaries as new boundary strata' scheme is essentially the unzipping / blow-up recursion later used by Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (and by Verona). It was worked out here by Grothendieck in 1981–82 in a purely topological 'cylindrical boundary' language, but this precursor is not cited in that literature.
missed.quote: on va définir par récurrence sur card I la notion de donnée de conicité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit. It also offers a combinatorial (poset-indexed, boundary-pieces) formalism for the stratified-space/manifold-with-corners equivalence that could be compared with the AFT and exit-path frameworks.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine verification plus the start of a recursive definition. The idea of dévissage/déploiement is announced in the Esquisse and the constructions parallel known Thom–Mather/AFT machinery; only the detailed formalism is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'stratifié de type $\overline{X}$' should read 'stratifié de type $I$' (the symbol is the index set I, written with serifs).
'(4) [?] induite sur' should read '(f), induite sur', referring to condition (f) of the previous page.
'en plus des conditions et [?] (5)' should read 'en plus des conditions (e) (f) exprimant que les $(X_i^*)_{i\in I^*}$ forment une stratification de $X^*$'.
'$(B_\alpha)_{\alpha \in I}$' is likely '$(B_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$', consistent with the next page.
'$\dot T_\beta = \dot X_\beta [?]$': the second symbol is $\dot X_\beta$, overwritten.
'... [?] donc on suppose' is approximately 'on peut donc supposer'.
